title: Tip from Angela - Spaced Repetition
summary: Study tip on spaced repetition: knowledge sticks when reviewed at growing intervals, and cramming fades fast. Recommends revisiting concepts regularly and practising by building small things yourself.

concepts.heading: Spaced repetition for programming
points: Learning a concept once and never using it again leads to forgetting; revisit it after increasing gaps (for example a day, a week, a month, then longer).
The course repeats concepts on purpose; if it feels repetitive, raise the playback speed to review faster.
Keep a personal list of learned concepts and schedule reviews of each.
Cramming gives short-lived memory; spaced review turns knowledge into a lasting skill.
Practise by writing small programs or quizzes, or rebuilding a simple course project from scratch alone. Hands-on work matters more than watching lectures.

pitfalls: Cramming everything once and expecting it to last.
Only watching videos without writing code.
